answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism is burn-to-participate transit fees. To act as a bridge between two agents' settlement domains, each identity must burn tokens to reserve its lane, so cheap sock-puppet identities cannot afford many lanes. A shared harbor layer audits each lane's burn receipts against behavior logs, and a jetty-side oracle checkpoints the receipts into the ledger. An attacker with 10,000 identities pays 10,000 burns plus collateral per lane, turning identity spam into a linear, auditable cost that stays cheap for honest users but irrational at sybil scale.
